newsitem.title: UK: Labour ex-Treasury minister sees party raising tax.
newsitem.headline: Labour ex-Treasury minister sees party raising tax.

text.p: A former Labour Chief Secretary to the Treasury said on Wednesday he believed that if the party returns to government it will have to raise taxes.
Lord Joel Barnett told Reuters he had made the point in a debate on the economy in the upper House of Lords.

"I certainly did say that," Barnett, who was a cabinet member under Prime Minister James Callaghan from 1977 to 1979, said. However, he said he was making no predictions about how much taxes would go up.
Barnett, said that although Labour leaders have pledged not to raise the basic rates of income tax, there were many ways of increasing the government's tax take without doing that.
He said he believed a Labour government would face a need to raise spending, and he hoped it would want to do so to improve health, education and other services.

But he said he did not blame Labour leaders for their pledges to keep taxes down. "I think they were bound to do this to counter the inevitable election attack on the party," he told Reuters. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
